candidates.original_title: Diverse somatic mutation patterns and pathway alterations in human cancers
candidates.description: Expression of the GNAO1 R243H mutation increases anchorage-independent colony formation compared with wild-type GNAO1 in human mammary epithelial cells.
candidates.citation_sentence: Using this technique, Kan and colleagues identified an uncharacterized somatic mutation in GNAO1 from breast carcinoma tissue (Kan et al., 2010). This key experiment reported that the R243H mutation promotes a two-fold increase in anchorage-independent growth compared to cells expressing wild type GNAO1, and will be replicated in Protocol 1.
candidates.notes: This is a registered replication protocol with no replication outcome reported; Protocol 3, rather than the expression-validation Protocol 2, is coded as the replication experiment. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Diverse somatic mutation patterns and pathway alterations in human cancers
candidates.description: Expression of the MAP2K4 R228K mutation increases anchorage-independent colony formation compared with wild-type MAP2K4 in NIH3T3 fibroblasts.
candidates.citation_sentence: In Figure 4C–E, the functional relevance of six select MAP2K4 mutants (5 located in the kinase domain, 1 outside the kinase domain) were tested in vitro (Kan et al., 2010). Importantly, all six MAP2K4 variants resulted in significantly enhanced agar colony formation compared to cells expressing wild type MAP2K4.
candidates.notes: This is a registered replication protocol with no replication outcome reported. Protocol 5 tests R228K and A279T separately. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Diverse somatic mutation patterns and pathway alterations in human cancers
candidates.description: The MAP2K4 R228K mutation reduces kinase activity toward JNK compared with wild-type MAP2K4.
candidates.citation_sentence: In Figure 4C–E, the functional relevance of six select MAP2K4 mutants (5 located in the kinase domain, 1 outside the kinase domain) were tested in vitro (Kan et al., 2010). A majority of the MAP2K4 mutants resulted in reduced activity to either JNK or myelin basic protein (MBP) when tested in an in vitro kinase assay suggesting that reduced MAP2K4 signaling plays a dominant-negative role in the control of cell growth.
candidates.notes: Protocol 6 is a planned replication of Figure 4F; no replication outcome is reported. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
